cues.en: Instructor: In this video, I'm going to tell you about a procedure called cross-validation.
cues.zh: 講師：這部影片介紹一個稱為交叉驗證的程序。

cues.en: This is kind of an alternative method to evaluating statistical significance that is different from the kind of traditional p-value-based hypothesis testing method.
cues.zh: 這算是評估統計顯著性的另一種方法，和傳統以 P 值為基礎的假設檢定不同。

cues.en: So in this video, I'm going to talk about it, tell you what it means, and explain how it works.
cues.zh: 會介紹它的意義，以及如何運作。

cues.en: And then in the next video, I'm going to discuss the differences between statistical significance versus classification accuracy.
cues.zh: 下一部影片再討論統計顯著性與分類準確率的差異。

cues.en: Okay, so let's talk about cross-validation.
cues.zh: 來談交叉驗證。

cues.en: So here, the idea is imagine this is all of your data.
cues.zh: 想像這是你所有的資料。

cues.en: This is just kind of representing all of the sample data that you have acquired in your experiment.
cues.zh: 代表實驗中取得的所有樣本資料。

cues.en: The idea is that you parcel it your data into this much.
cues.zh: 概念是，分出這麼多資料。

cues.en: So you take this much data, let's say that's 90% of your data, and you generate some statistical model.
cues.zh: 取這部分，假設是 90%，建立某種統計模型。

cues.en: Maybe it's a regression model, a hierarchical linear model, maybe it's a correlation-based model.
cues.zh: 也許是迴歸、階層線性模型，或以相關為基礎的模型。

cues.en: It doesn't really matter for the purposes of this video.
cues.zh: 就這部影片而言，不重要。

cues.en: The point is you come up with some model, some set of equations that characterizes the dynamics in your data.
cues.zh: 重點是提出模型、一組方程式，描述資料中的動態。

cues.en: So you construct the model, statistical model on these data, ignoring these data altogether.
cues.zh: 用這些資料建立統計模型，完全忽略那些資料。

cues.en: So the data over here never actually get into the statistical model.
cues.zh: 那邊的資料不會進入統計模型。

cues.en: And then once you've constructed your statistical model, then what you do is apply the model to these data.
cues.zh: 模型建立後，再套用到那些資料。

cues.en: Now, this is the pretty interesting setup because the data that the model used to tune the parameters and so on are different from the data
cues.zh: 這個設定很有趣，因為用來調整參數的資料，和實際

cues.en: that are actually being put into the model.
cues.zh: 送進模型評估的資料不同。

cues.en: So in the parlance of machine learning and statistics and cross-validation, these data here are called the training set or the training data.
cues.zh: 在機器學習、統計和交叉驗證的術語中，這些叫訓練集，或訓練資料。

cues.en: These are the data that you use to create your statistical model.
cues.zh: 用來建立統計模型。

cues.en: And here, we have the test set.
cues.zh: 這裡則是測試集。

cues.en: This is called the test set.
cues.zh: 稱為測試集。

cues.en: So training set, used to create the model; and the test set, used to evaluate the performance of the model.
cues.zh: 訓練集用來建立模型，測試集用來評估表現。

cues.en: You could also call this in-sample data and out-of-sample data.
cues.zh: 也可以稱為樣本內資料、樣本外資料。

cues.en: These are just different terms for the same idea.
cues.zh: 只是相同概念的不同術語。

cues.en: Now, there's nothing particularly special about these data over here that we drop them from the training set.
cues.zh: 從訓練集排除的這些資料，其實沒有特別之處。

cues.en: So in fact, what you want to do in cross-validation is treat this procedure that I just explained as one iteration through the cross-validation procedure.
cues.zh: 所以交叉驗證中，剛才解釋的程序只是其中一次迭代。

cues.en: So you repeat this idea, but then you're using a different set of data for training and a different set for testing.
cues.zh: 重複這個想法，但換不同的訓練資料與測試資料。

cues.en: And again, there's nothing particularly special about the first 10% of your data to be reserved for the testing set.
cues.zh: 保留最前面 10% 作測試，也沒有特別之處。

cues.en: So you repeat this over the next 10% of your data and so on.
cues.zh: 再對下一個 10% 重複，依此類推。

cues.en: So you keep repeating this until eventually, all of the data are being used for the model and all of the data are being used for testing, but in different runs,
cues.zh: 不斷重複，最後所有資料都用來建模，也都用來測試，但在不同執行、

cues.en: in different iterations of cross-validation.
cues.zh: 不同交叉驗證迭代中。

cues.en: This is called K-fold cross-validation, where the number of times that you go through and leave out part of your data and reserve it for testing, that is the number K.
cues.zh: 這叫 K 折交叉驗證，每次排除一部分資料並保留測試，這樣的次數就是 K。

cues.en: So for example, if each time you go through, you leave out 10% of the data, then it takes you 10 iterations, 10 times to go through this,
cues.zh: 例如每次排除 10%，就要做 10 次迭代，

cues.en: construct the model, apply the model to the test data, and then keep going with the next chunk of data.
cues.zh: 建立模型、套用到測試資料，再處理下一塊。

cues.en: So 10% of your data leaving out, it takes 10 times to get through all the data.
cues.zh: 每次排除 10%，要 10 次才能走過全部資料。

cues.en: That would be called 10-fold cross-validation.
cues.zh: 就叫十折交叉驗證。

cues.en: And if you do it 13 times, you know, you cut up your data into 13 equally-sized chunks, then it would be called 13-fold cross-validation.
cues.zh: 如果做 13 次，把資料分成 13 個等大區塊，就叫十三折交叉驗證。

cues.en: So what's an appropriate K?
cues.zh: K 多少適當？

cues.en: Well, you know, there's no real right or wrong answer.
cues.zh: 沒有真正的對錯答案。

cues.en: You can get poor results from going to either extreme.
cues.zh: 走向任何一個極端，都可能得到差的結果。

cues.en: So if you only have like two-fold cross-validation, that's not so bad.
cues.zh: 只有二折，其實也不太差。

cues.en: That's called split half for liability.
cues.zh: 這稱為折半信度。

cues.en: So you split your data into 50% and 50%, but generally your results are gonna be more robust if you use a higher value of K.
cues.zh: 把資料分成 50%、50%，但通常 K 高一點，結果會更穩健。

cues.en: On the other hand, if K starts to get really high, like, you know, 100-fold cross-validation, these individual bins might end up being pretty small.
cues.zh: 另一方面，如果 K 很高，例如百折，每個個別區間可能很小。

cues.en: So the accuracy might be also sort of unstable.
cues.zh: 準確率可能不穩定。

cues.en: You might be driven by too much noise and sampling variability.
cues.zh: 可能受到太多雜訊和抽樣變異影響。

cues.en: So there isn't really a correct answer, but usually somewhere around 10 to 20 is a pretty typical range for K for K-fold cross-validation.
cues.zh: 所以沒有正確答案，但通常 K 在 10 到 20 左右相當常見。

cues.en: Now, there isn't like some deep, meaningful, age-old mathematical statistical theory that says that 10 to 20 is the optimal value of K.
cues.zh: 沒有什麼深奧、有意義、歷史悠久的數學統計理論，說 10 到 20 是最佳值。

cues.en: These are the kinds of parameters that people have just discovered based on playing around with data, exploring a bunch of different values of K.
cues.zh: 這些參數是大家透過資料嘗試、探索不同 K 值後發現的。

cues.en: And, you know, just some experience indicates that somewhere around 10 to 20-fold cross-validation tends to be a pretty good number.
cues.zh: 經驗上，大概十折到二十折往往不錯。

cues.en: So here, I'm illustrating reserving your test data in a block.
cues.zh: 這裡把測試資料保留成一整塊。

cues.en: So this is like a contiguous block of data.
cues.zh: 一個連續的資料區塊。

cues.en: Now, thing is with cross-validation, you want to avoid any biases in the training set or in the testing set.
cues.zh: 交叉驗證中，希望避免訓練集或測試集有任何偏差。

cues.en: So typically, you want to make sure that the data are actually drawn randomly from your entire dataset.
cues.zh: 通常要確保資料是從整個資料集隨機抽取。

cues.en: That prevents any biases that might occur if there's something different about the beginning of the data or something special about the end of the dataset.
cues.zh: 避免資料開頭或結尾有特殊性，導致偏差。

cues.en: So this is how I'm depicting it here.
cues.zh: 所以這裡這樣表示。

cues.en: Normally, it would be something a little bit more like this where you're taking 10% of the data, but it's drawn randomly from throughout the entire dataset.
cues.zh: 通常比較像這樣，取 10% 資料，但從整個資料集隨機抽出。

cues.en: Now, whether this step is really necessary depends on the organization of your data.
cues.zh: 這一步是否必要，取決於資料組織方式。

cues.en: Maybe the data are already totally organized, totally randomly sorted, in the dataset you have.
cues.zh: 也許資料集本來就完全隨機排序。

cues.en: And in that case, it might be just practically easier in terms of the code to do it in contiguous chunks like this.
cues.zh: 這時就程式實作而言，像這樣取連續區塊可能更方便。

cues.en: But it's important to keep in mind that in general, you want your training set and your testing set to be randomly distributed throughout the dataset to avoid introducing any systematic biases
cues.zh: 但要記住，一般希望訓練集和測試集隨機分布在整個資料集中，避免引入系統性偏差，

cues.en: if there is some kind of correlation structure, if there's some meaningful relationships between neighboring data points here.
cues.zh: 如果相鄰資料點有某種相關結構、有意義的關係。

cues.en: So cross-validation has a couple of uses, it has a couple of applications.
cues.zh: 交叉驗證有幾種用途、應用。

cues.en: One of those is to estimate the...
cues.zh: 其中一種是估計……

cues.en: or to compute the variance of an estimate.
cues.zh: 或者計算估計值的變異數。

cues.en: This is also called confidence intervals.
cues.zh: 這也稱為信賴區間。

cues.en: You will learn more about this in a later section on the course on computing confidence intervals.
cues.zh: 後面計算信賴區間那一章，會學更多。

cues.en: And there, it's actually often called jack-knifing.
cues.zh: 那裡經常稱為刀切法。

cues.en: So I'll explain a procedure called jack-knifing, which is basically what I'm doing here with cross-validation.
cues.zh: 會解釋刀切法程序，基本上和這裡的交叉驗證類似。

cues.en: It's very simple, similar contrast, although it's not exactly the same thing as cross-validation, but it's very similar procedure.
cues.zh: 概念非常類似，雖然不完全相同，但程序很接近。

cues.en: So the idea of jack-knifing is to compute estimates based on part of your data, and then you keep recomputing those estimates based on different parts of your data,
cues.zh: 刀切法的概念，是用部分資料計算估計值，再用不同部分重新計算，

cues.en: and that allows you to gain some confidence or compute these mathematical confidence intervals around some estimate, for example, the mean, or the variance, or entropy,
cues.zh: 讓你對平均值、變異數、熵，或其他估計值取得一些信心，或計算數學上的信賴區間，

cues.en: or whatever it is you are testing about a dataset.
cues.zh: 不管你要檢驗資料集的什麼性質。

cues.en: Another use of cross-validation is to avoid biases in your analysis results, and that's because you are applying the model to data it has never seen.
cues.zh: 另一種用途是避免分析結果偏誤，因為把模型套用到從未見過的資料。

cues.en: So if there is some overfitting that's happening in the training dataset, that overfitting in the training data actually reduces performance in the test set.
cues.zh: 如果訓練資料過度擬合，就會降低測試集表現。

cues.en: So in fact, your models will do better on the test set when they're not overfitting the training dataset.
cues.zh: 所以沒有過度擬合訓練集的模型，在測試集會表現更好。

cues.en: So this is why it's one way to avoid introducing biases into your analysis results.
cues.zh: 這就是避免分析結果引入偏差的一種方式。

cues.en: Now, I'll qualify this a little bit in the next slide because it's a bit tricky to make sure that you are really avoiding biases in training and test sets.
cues.zh: 下一張會稍作補充，因為確保訓練、測試集真正避免偏差，有點棘手。

cues.en: And another use of cross-validation, which, I think, is probably the most common use, the most common reason why people apply cross-validation,
cues.zh: 另一種用途，我想也是最常見、大家使用交叉驗證最常見的原因，

cues.en: is to compute something called classification accuracy.
cues.zh: 是計算所謂分類準確率。

cues.en: So the idea here is that we want to classify our data as being in group A or group C.
cues.zh: 想把資料分類為 A 組或 C 組。

cues.en: In deep learning, we often are interested in image classification.
cues.zh: 深度學習中，經常對影像分類有興趣。

cues.en: So we want to know: Is this image, you know, is it a picture of a turkey or a sheep?
cues.zh: 例如想知道，這張圖是火雞還是綿羊？

cues.en: And so we can classify, we can have the model classify the the dataset, and we can compute accuracy in the test set.
cues.zh: 讓模型分類資料，再計算測試集的準確率。

cues.en: Okay, just a quick word about the independence of the training and the testing datasets.
cues.zh: 簡單談一下訓練集和測試集的獨立性。

cues.en: So ideally, the test set is really, truly, actually independent of the training set, but you have to keep in mind that that's not necessarily always the case
cues.zh: 理想上，測試集真的、確實獨立於訓練集，但要記住，不一定只因為

cues.en: just because you are separating the data.
cues.zh: 分開資料，就能如此。

cues.en: So independence of the test set and the training set helps avoid biases, it helps avoid overfitting.
cues.zh: 獨立性有助避免偏差、過度擬合。

cues.en: However, this independence between the training data and the testing data is not necessarily trivially true in all datasets just because you're separating the data.
cues.zh: 但不是所有資料集，只要分開，訓練資料和測試資料就自然獨立。

cues.en: So imagine, we have...
cues.zh: 想像……

cues.en: Our sample contains a group of self-selected students from the same school.
cues.zh: 樣本是一群來自同一學校、自願參與的學生。

cues.en: So maybe you're doing some research about academic performance in high schools and you have a a group, your sample is students who are on the basketball team
cues.zh: 也許研究高中學業表現，樣本卻是籃球隊的學生，

cues.en: and who also like to watch sci-fi movies, I don't know.
cues.zh: 而且也喜歡看科幻電影之類的。

cues.en: So that's a pretty narrow group of individuals.
cues.zh: 這是很狹窄的一群人。

cues.en: So you can take your 30 students and break them up into 27 for training data and three for the testing data.
cues.zh: 可以把 30 位學生分成 27 位訓練、3 位測試。

cues.en: Now, technically, you are separating the training data and the testing data.
cues.zh: 技術上，確實分開訓練和測試資料。

cues.en: However, the training data are not really independent of the test data, and that's because they're already very similar to each other even before you separated them.
cues.zh: 但它們不真正獨立，因為分開之前，就已非常相似。

cues.en: Another example would be if you are doing cross-validation on time-series analysis, and what you find very often in time-series signals is that they have some auto-correlation structure.
cues.zh: 另一個例子是時間序列分析的交叉驗證，時間序列訊號常有自相關結構。

cues.en: So you have time-series data that's kind of going up and down, and the data point or the value at one data point is strongly correlated with the data points at neighboring values.
cues.zh: 資料上下變動，而某個資料點的值，和相鄰資料點強烈相關。

cues.en: So there, because the data have a rich auto-correlation structure, then even when you separate in randomly selected data points,
cues.zh: 因為具有豐富自相關結構，即使隨機分出資料點，

cues.en: they're still going to be very strongly correlated with the training data because the test data and the training data all come from the same dataset that have a strong correlation in them.
cues.zh: 仍然和訓練資料高度相關，因為測試和訓練來自同個強相關資料集。

cues.en: Anyway, this is just something to be mindful.
cues.zh: 總之，這值得留意。

cues.en: It is not necessarily trivially the case that your testing set data is independent of the training set data.
cues.zh: 測試集資料不一定自然獨立於訓練集。

cues.en: Okay, so in this video, I introduced you to the idea of cross-validation and the terms training set and testing set.
cues.zh: 這部影片介紹交叉驗證，以及訓練集、測試集術語。

cues.en: In the next video, I will continue this discussion by talking about the differences between statistical significance and classification accuracy.
cues.zh: 下一部會繼續，談統計顯著性和分類準確率的差異。
